title: Eruption of Mount Mazama
summary: Mount Mazama, a cluster of overlapping Cascade volcanoes, was destroyed by an enormous explosive eruption about 7,700 years ago. So much molten rock was expelled that the summit collapsed into a caldera, which later filled with water to form Crater Lake, the deepest lake in the United States. Ash fell over much of the western United States and southwestern Canada, covering about 1.7 million km2.

uncertainty.note: Both sources say "7,700 years ago", with no calendar year or error given. The year -5677 is an approximate conversion from 7,700 years ago (reference year 2023) and the id; treat it as rounded to the century.

beats.caption: A towering column of pumice and ash begins the eruption that destroys the Mount Mazama volcanic cluster.
Ash settles over the western United States and southwestern Canada, blanketing about 1.7 million square kilometres.
The summit collapses into a caldera that fills with water as Crater Lake; the ash becomes a stratigraphic marker.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the year -5677 is a conversion from "7,700 years ago", with no sourced error. The caldera is 8 x 10 km per NPS, so the point is the Wikidata location of Mount Mazama with a 10 km uncertainty. Whether "Oregon" is stated on the pages was not used in the summary.
